stem: A coil consists of 400 turns of wire. Each turn is a square of side \(d = 20\) cm. A uniform magnetic field directed perpendicular to the plane of the coil is turned on. If the field changes linearly from 0 to 0.50 T in 0.8 s, what is the magnitude of induced emf in the coil while the field is changing?
solution:
The magnitude of induced emf in the coil is written as

\(|e| = \left| \dfrac{\mathrm{d}(N\phi)}{\mathrm{d}t} \right| = N \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(\because \phi = B \cdot A\)

\(\therefore |e| = N \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}(BA)}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(= N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) (as \(A\) is constant and \(B\) is changing with time)

\(= N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{\Delta B}{\Delta t} = N \cdot A \cdot \dfrac{B_{\text{final}} - B_{\text{initial}}}{\Delta t}\)

Inserting the given values of \(N = 400\), \(A = (20\ \text{cm})^2 = (0.2\ \text{m})^2\), \(B_{\text{final}} = 0.5\) T, \(B_{\text{initial}} = 0\), \(\Delta t = 0.8\) s, we find the induced emf

\(|e| = \dfrac{400 \cdot (0.20\ \text{m})^2 (0.5\ \text{T})}{0.8\ \text{s}}\)

\(= 10\) Volt

subtopic: Induced emf in a Stationary Coil
stem: A long solenoid S, as shown in the figure has 200 turns/cm and carries a current \(i\) of 1.4 A. The diameter \(D\) of the solenoid is 3 cm. A coil C, having 100 turns and diameter \(d\) of 2 cm is kept coaxial to the solenoid. The current in the solenoid is decreased steadily to zero in 20 ms. Calculate the magnitude of emf induced in the coil C when the current in the solenoid is changing.
solution:
Part of magnetic flux (per turn) of the solenoid S that links with the coil C is

\(\phi_{\text{c}} = \mu_0\, n_{\text{s}}\, i\, \dfrac{\pi\, \mathrm{d}_{\text{c}}^{2}}{4}\)

This flux reduces to zero in \(\mathrm{d}t = 20\) ms. Thus, the emf induced in coil C of \(N_{\text{c}}\) turns is

\(e_{\text{s}} = -N_{\text{c}} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi_{\text{c}}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{-(0 - \phi_{\text{c}})}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\mu_0 N_{\text{c}} n_{\text{s}} i \pi\, \mathrm{d}_{\text{c}}^{2}}{4\,\mathrm{d}t}\)

\(= \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100 \times 2 \times 10^{4} \times 1.4 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}}{4 \times 20 \times 10^{-3}}\)

\(= 55.24\) mV

subtopic: Generators, Back emf and Energy Transfer
stem: A rotating armature of a simple generator consists of rectangular section DABC of a conducting wire as shown in the figure, to which connections are made through sliding contacts. The armature is rotated at 1500 rpm in the magnetic field \((\vec{B})\) of 0.5 N/A.m. Determine the induced emf between the terminals P and Q of the generator at the instant shown in the adjoining figure.
solution:
The wire AB (\(l = 10\) cm) is moving to the right with the tangential velocity v.

\(\left| \vec{\mathrm{v}} \right| = \left| \vec{\omega} \times \vec{r} \right|\)

v \(= \omega r\) where \(\omega\) is angular velocity and \(r\) is the radius.

\(\mathrm{v} = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \cdot r\)  \(\left[ \because \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} \right]\)

\(= 2\pi \nu r\)

\(= 2\pi \cdot \left( \dfrac{1500}{60\,\mathrm{s}} \right) \cdot \left( \dfrac{4}{100} \right) \mathrm{m}\)  \(\left[ \because r = AD = (4/100)\,\mathrm{m} \right]\)

\(= 2\pi\) m/s

\(= 6.284\) m/s

The magnetic field is directed vertically upward from North to South pole. As the wire AB is cutting the magnetic lines of force perpendicularly, the induced emf is, therefore, maximum.

\(\because e = Bl\mathrm{v} \sin\theta\) with \(\theta = 90^\circ\),

Then, \(e = e_{\max} = Bl\mathrm{v}\)

\(= (0.5\ \text{N/A.m})\,(10/100)\,\text{m} \cdot (6.28\ \text{m/s})\)

\(= \dfrac{0.5}{10} \times 6.28\)

\(= 0.314\) V

or \(e_{\max} \approx 314.2\) mV.

The emf induced in the wires BC and DA is zero because the magnetic Lorentz force on free electrons in these wire \(\left[ \vec{F} = q(\vec{\mathrm{v}} \times \vec{B}) \right]\) has no component parallel to the wires. Also there is no e.m.f. in the lead in wires, which are stationary and are not in motion \((\vec{\mathrm{v}} = 0)\). Therefore the total emf between the terminals P and Q is due the movement of segment AB. i.e., \(e = 314\) mV. The direction of induced emf is given by Lenz's law.

stem: A conducting loop of area 1 m\(^2\) is placed normal to uniform magnetic field 3 Wb/m\(^2\). If the magnetic field is uniformly reduced to 1 Wb/m\(^2\) in a time of 0.5 s, calculate the induced emf produced in the loop.
solution:
Given,

Area of the loop, \(A = 1\) m\(^2\)

\((B)_{\text{initial}} = 3\) Wb/m\(^2\)

\((B)_{\text{final}} = 1\) Wb/m\(^2\)

duration of time, \(\Delta t = 0.5\) s

\(\therefore\) Induced emf,

\(|e| = \left| \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t} \right| = \left| \dfrac{\phi_{\text{final}} - \phi_{\text{initial}}}{\text{Time interval}} \right|\)

\(= \dfrac{(B_{\text{final}} - B_{\text{initial}})A}{\Delta t}\)

\(= \left| \left[ \dfrac{(1-3)}{0.5} \cdot 1 \right] \right|\) volt

\(= \left| -\dfrac{2}{0.5} \cdot 1 \right|\) volt

\(|e| = 4\) volt

subtopic: Self-Inductance and Energy in a Magnetic Field
stem: Derive an expression for the self-inductance of a toroid of circular cross-section of radius \(r\) and major radius \(R\). Calculate the self inductance \((L)\) of toroid for major radius \((R) = 15\) cm, cross-section of toroid having radius \((r) = 2.0\) cm and the number of turns \((n) = 1200\).
solution:
The magnetic field inside a toroid,

\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2\pi r_0}\), where \(N\) is the number of turns and \(r_0\) is the distance from the toroidal axis. If \(r << R\), we can use \(r_0 \cong R\). Hence,

\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i}{2\,u\,R}\)

The magnetic flux \((\phi)\) passing through cavity is

\(\phi = \left( \pi r^2 \right) \dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi} \dfrac{Ni}{R} = \dfrac{\mu_0 N i r^2}{2R}\)

This is the flux that links each turn. When the current \(i\) varies with time, the induced emf \(e\) across the terminals of toroid is given by Faraday's law.

\(e = -\dfrac{N \mathrm{d}\phi}{\mathrm{d}t} = -N \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 N i r^2}{2R} \right)\)

\(e = -N \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 N r^2}{2R} \right) \dfrac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

Comparing with \(e = -L \dfrac{\mathrm{d}i}{\mathrm{d}t}\)

We get,

\(L = \dfrac{\mu_0}{2} \dfrac{N^2 r^2}{R}\)   \((\because r << R)\)

Given,

\(N = 1200\), \(r = 2.0\) cm, \(R = 15\) cm and \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\) T.m/A.

\(L = 2.414 \times 10^{-3}\) H

subtopic: Self-Inductance and Energy in a Magnetic Field
stem: Consider a uniformly wound solenoid having \(N\) turns and length \(l\). The core of the solenoid is air. Find the inductance of the solenoid of \(N = 200\), \(l = 20\) cm and cross-sectional area, \(A = 5\) cm\(^2\). Calculate the induced emf \(e_{\mathrm{L}}\), if the current flowing through the solenoid decreases at a rate of 60 A/s.
solution:
The magnetic flux through each turn of area \(A\) in the solenoid is

\(\phi_B = B \cdot A = (\mu_0 n i) \cdot A\)  \((\because\) Magnetic field inside a solenoid is \(B = \mu_0 ni)\)

\(= \mu_0 (N/l) \cdot i \cdot A\)  \((\because n\) is the number of turns per unit length \(= N/l)\)

We know that the inductance \((L)\) of the solenoid can be written as

\(L = (N \phi_B)/i\)

Substituting the value of \(\phi_B\), we get

\(L = (N/i) \cdot \{ \mu_0 \cdot (N/l) \cdot i \cdot A \}\)

\(L = \mu_0 \cdot (N^2/l) \cdot A\)

Inserting the given values of \(N\), \(l\) and \(A\), we find

\(L = (4\pi \cdot 10^{-7}\,\text{Tm}/A) \cdot (200)^2 (5 \cdot 10^{-4}\,\text{m}^2)/(20 \cdot 10^{-4}\,\text{m})\)

or \(L \approx 0.1257\) mH

The induced emf in the solenoid

\(e_{\mathrm{L}} = -L\,(\mathrm{d}i/\mathrm{d}t)\)

\(e_{\mathrm{L}} = -(0.126 \cdot 10^{-3})\,(-60\ \text{A/s}) = 7.543\) mV

subtopic: Self-Inductance and Energy in a Magnetic Field
stem: The self-inductance of a closely wound coil of 200 turns is 10 mH. Determine the value of magnetic flux through the cross-section of the coil when the current passing through the coil is 4 mA.
solution:
Given :

Self-inductance of coil, \(L = 10\) mH,

Number of turns, \(N = 200\), and

Current through the coil, \(i = 4\) mA

The total value of magnetic flux \(\phi\) associated with the coil is,

\(\phi = L\,i\)

\(= (10 \times 10^{-3})\ \text{H} \times (4 \times 10^{-3})\ \text{A}\)

\(= 4 \times 10^{-5}\) Wb

The flux per turn (or flux through the cross-section of the coil)

\(= \dfrac{\phi}{N}\)

\(= \left( \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{Wb}}{200} \right)\)

\(= 2 \times 10^{-7}\) Wb

subtopic: Self-Inductance and Energy in a Magnetic Field
stem: Calculate the self-inductance of a coaxial cable of length \(l\) and carrying a current \(I\). The current flows down the inner cylinder with radius \(a\), and flows out of the outer cylinder with radius \(b\).
solution:
According to Ampere's law, the magnetic field \((B)\) between two cylinders at a distance \(r\) from the axis is given by

\(B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\).

The magnetic field is zero elsewhere.

We also know that the magnetic energy density,

\(u_B = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0} = \dfrac{1}{2\mu_0} \left( \dfrac{\mu_0^2 I^2}{4\pi^2 r^2} \right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{8\pi^2 r^2}\)

Energy stored in a cylindrical shell of length \(l\), radius \(r\) and thickness \(\mathrm{d}r\) is given by

\(\left( \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{8\pi^2 r^2} \right) \times 2\pi l r\, \mathrm{d}r = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2 l}{4\pi} \left( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}r}{r} \right)\)

Integrating from \(a\) to \(b\), we get

\(W = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2 l}{4\pi} \ln \left( \dfrac{b}{a} \right)\)

Magnetic energy confined in an inductor \((L)\) carrying a current \((I)\) can also be written as \(\dfrac{1}{2} L I^2\). Comparing the two expressions we find the inductance of coaxial cable as

\(L = \dfrac{\mu_0 l}{2\pi} \ln \left( \dfrac{b}{a} \right)\)

stem:
Mutual inductance of the wireless charging system.

In a wireless battery charger, the base unit can be imagined as a solenoid (coil B) of length \(l\) with \(N_{\mathrm{B}}\) turns, carrying a current \(i_{\mathrm{B}}\) and having a cross-section area \(A\). The handle coil (coil \(H\)) has \(N_{\mathrm{H}}\) turns and surrounds the base solenoid (coil B) completely. The base unit is designed to hold the handle of the charging unit. The handle has a cylindrical hole so that it fits loosely over a matching cylinder on the base unit. When the handle is placed on the base, the current flowing in coil \(B\) induces a current in the coil \(H\). Thus, the induced current in the coil \(H\) is used to charge the battery housed in the handle.
solution:
The magnetic field due to a solenoid coil B,

\(B_{\text{solenoid}} = \mu_0\, n\, i = \mu_0 \left( \dfrac{N_{\mathrm{B}}}{l} \right) i\)

Magnetic flux through coil \(H\) caused by the magnetic field \(B_{\text{solenoid}}\) due to solenoid coil B,

\(\phi_{\mathrm{H}} = B_{\text{solenoid}}\, A\)

Flux linkage \(= N_{\mathrm{H}} \phi_{\mathrm{H}}\)

The mutual inductance \((M)\) of the wireless charging system,

\(M = \dfrac{N_H B_{\text{solenoid}} A}{i} = \mu_0 \left( \dfrac{N_{\mathrm{B}}}{l} \right) A . N_H\)

\(= \mu_0 \left( \dfrac{N_{\mathrm{B}} N_{\mathrm{H}}}{l} \right) A\)
